didYouKnow: Cardiovascular disease kills more people than all cancers combined.
Over 75% of CVD deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries.
90% of stroke cases are potentially preventable with risk factor management.
High BMI now accounts for nearly 1 in 10 of all cardiovascular deaths globally.

faq.q: How many people die from heart disease each year?
faq.a: An estimated 19.8 million people died from cardiovascular diseases in 2022, representing approximately 32% of all global deaths — making CVD the world's leading cause of death.

faq.q: What is the difference between heart disease and cardiovascular disease?
faq.a: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is an umbrella term covering all heart and blood vessel diseases, including coronary heart disease, stroke, heart failure, and hypertension.

faq.q: How many people have high blood pressure?
faq.a: Approximately 1.33 billion adults worldwide have hypertension, but only 21% have it adequately controlled.

faq.q: What percentage of heart disease is preventable?
faq.a: WHO estimates that 80% of premature heart attacks and strokes are preventable through lifestyle changes and risk factor management.

faq.q: Which country has the highest heart disease mortality?
faq.a: Eastern European and Central Asian countries like Uzbekistan, Ukraine, and Russia have the highest age-standardized CVD mortality rates globally.
